description: Teams keep their own channel reports in Excel and do not use the new platform, so the silos stay (the brief warns about resistance to giving up channel-specific reporting)
mitigation: Map every existing channel report to the Power BI report that replaces it, then retire them one by one with a date agreed by general management; one data champion per department

description: Customers cannot be matched reliably across POS loyalty, e-commerce, CRM and support (missing or different emails, duplicates), so the single customer view and the segments are wrong
mitigation: Define matching rules and data stewards in phase 1; measure the match rate with dbt tests and only start segmentation when it reaches the agreed target

description: The platform depends on 0.5 of an internal data engineer and on consultants who leave after the build; if that person leaves, nobody can maintain the pipelines
mitigation: Recruit or train the internal engineer before the build starts and pair them with the consultant; all logic kept in documented dbt models; a second person trained as back-up

description: Build takes more consultant days than our estimates (Part 3), so the budget is exceeded
mitigation: Fixed scope and a go/no-go gate for each use case; a 15 % contingency (about 39 kEUR on top of the 257 kEUR of Part 3); Part 3 shows +50 % build days adds about 33 kEUR and does not change the choice

description: Personal data (customers, web-analytics tracking) is processed without a valid consent or kept too long; GDPR fines can reach 20 MEUR or 4 % of turnover
mitigation: Data protection impact assessment before segmentation; raw layer restricted to IT; consent flag carried into the customer tables; retention periods and an erasure procedure; EU region only

description: Vendors raise prices (Power BI Pro went from 10 to 14 USD in April 2025; Fivetran changed its pricing in 2025 and 2026)
mitigation: 1-year reservations and annual contracts; transformations in dbt so they can move platform; Airbyte kept as back-up for Fivetran

description: Microsoft Fabric is young: some features are in preview and the dbt adapter for the Fabric lakehouse is not generally available yet
mitigation: Use the Fabric Warehouse with its supported dbt adapter; no preview features in production

description: Store connections are unreliable, so POS data from some of the 30 stores arrives late or incomplete
mitigation: Load POS data in small batches with retries; freshness tests per store; daily reconciliation with ERP sales totals

description: Sources refresh at different frequencies (POS during the day, ERP once a day), so numbers differ between reports and users stop trusting them
mitigation: Show the last refresh time on every report; one business glossary (net revenue, order, channel); reconcile sales with ERP finance

description: Business users do not have the skills for self-service analytics (only 10 report creators are trained)
mitigation: PL-300 training for creators, workshops for readers, office hours with the data champions in the first months

description: The ERP turns out to be SAP Business One, not Business Central, so Fabric loses its main advantage (Part 1 section 7)
mitigation: Confirm the ERP at the start of the project; if it is SAP Business One, ask Snowflake, BigQuery and Microsoft for quotes before choosing

description: The expected benefit does not arrive: inventory optimization must recover about 2.3 % of inventory losses for the project to pay back (Part 3)
mitigation: Measure stock-outs and overstock before phase 2 to have a baseline; follow them monthly with the supply chain team; review the project at each gate
